rewayatInfo.title: About Rewayat
rewayatInfo.explanation:
A Rewayah (رواية, plural: Rewayat رِوَايَات) is a specific method of reciting the Quran that represents a particular transmission route within a larger Qira'at (قِرَاءَة, plural: Qira'at قِرَاءَات) tradition.

While Qira'at are the major schools of Quranic recitation attributed to famous reciters, Rewayat are the specific ways these recitations were transmitted through chains of narrators back to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

"The Quran was revealed in seven ahruf (styles). So recite what is easier for you from it."
- Sahih al-Bukhari 2419, Sahih Muslim 818

The most widely used Rewayah today is Hafs 'an Assem (حَفْص عَن عَاصِم), which is considered the standard version used in most printed Qurans and is instantly recognizable to most Muslims worldwide.

Each Rewayah may have slight variations in pronunciation, elongation, or articulation points. These differences are purely phonetic and never alter the meaning of the Quranic text, as they all represent authentic ways of reciting the Quran that have been meticulously preserved.

irab.tapWord: Tap a word to see its i'rab
irab.sources: Word i'rab generated from The Quranic Treebank (built on the Quranic Arabic Corpus, University of Leeds) and cross-checked word by word against MASAQ (University of Jordan). Where the two read a word differently, the other reading is shown as «وجه آخر». Morphology (root, pattern, verb form, number and gender) is from the same corpus; occurrence counts are over the whole Quran. Shown for the Hafs text.
irab.booksNote: Each passage is the page of the book that discusses this verse, so it can also cover the verses around it.
irab.noBooks: These books have no passage for this verse.

rasm.title: Rasm

note.hadhf: {{letter}} is not written in the mushaf.
note.badal: {{standard}} is written as {{mushaf}} in the mushaf.
note.hamz: The hamza is written {{mushaf}} in the mushaf and {{standard}} in the standard spelling.
note.wasl: Written as one word in the mushaf; the standard spelling separates it.
note.fasl: Written apart in the mushaf; the standard spelling joins the words.

rasm.sources: Standard spelling from {{source}}. The differences come from comparing it letter by letter with the mushaf's spelling; only those that the mushaf's own signs, a known spelling rule or a review confirm are shown. Shown for the Hafs text.
